title: The quadratic control and the callers could pass under the 20 ms floor on a host fast enough, because the run length was fixed
resolution: The helper doubles both runs until the short median reaches 20 ms, up to 2^24 characters, and takes an injected timer; scripted readings test the doubling, floor, and limit, with a fail-before, and the spec scenarios follow.

title: Importing the package set the expose-gc flag and made a VM context in every importer, unlike the design's claim
resolution: gc is exposed on the first timing with the default timer; a test that only imports the package checks that gc stays undefined, with a fail-before, and design.md states the scope.

title: The record gave a growth of 1.25 where the floored metric of the assertion was 0.25
resolution: The record separates raw ratios from floored scores, gives the measured maximum score of the new helper, and calls the results consistent with linear scaling over the tested inputs.

title: The default timer needs process.threadCpuUsage of Node.js 23.9 while the package declares >=22, and failed on older Node.js with a TypeError and no hint
resolution: The default timer asserts that process.threadCpuUsage exists and fails with 'assertLinearOnRuns needs Node.js 23.9 or later'; a test removes it, with a fail-before, and design.md names the requirement.

title: The requirement, proposal, and comment said the runs double until the run reaches 2^24 characters, while they stop when doubling would pass it
resolution: The requirement (498 characters, archive probed), the proposal, and the comment of timeUnit say the runs double until doubling the long run would pass 2^24 characters.

title: The record gave no suite-level runtime cost of the slower linear-time tests
resolution: verification.md records a measured make test run before and after: the Node.js suite took 288.0 and 305.1 s, the five callers 0.96 and 68.3 s; cheaper variants are listed as a follow-up only.

title: assertLinearOnRuns took two optional positional parameters, and SHORT_RUN_SHARE read as a fraction while it is a divisor
resolution: The helper takes an optional LinearTimeOptions object { length, timeRun }, the three calls with a length and the helper's tests pass it, and the constant is LENGTH_RATIO.

title: The limitation did not state which superlinear growth passes the limit of 2.5
resolution: verification.md's limitation and design.md's 'Growth, not an absolute limit' state the boundary exponent log4(10), about 1.66: n^1.5 passes and n^1.7 fails.
